Stop-Motion Paper Collage

Photocopied dashboards, torn scraps, halftone dots and cut-out ransom-note words on kraft, animated on twos with hard paper shadows. Teal and coral arrive as misregistered riso ink, and the anomaly is literally snipped out of the sheet and replaced by a circled clipping.

Tagline words slap in two per beat; the coral “Start free” scrap is pinned on the final downbeat while everything keeps its ±1 px boil.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Torn-edge mask — jagged clip-path per scrap with a hard offset paper shadow
  • Halftone photocopy — dot-screen background + high-contrast grain in multiply
  • Ransom-note words — each headline word on its own scrap, mixed serif / sans / ink
  • Riso block — flat teal + coral ink passes with a 6–8 px misregister
  • Snipped hole — the cut-out value, dashed outline showing kraft behind — the anomaly
  • Label-tape + pin — embossed black tape for the timestamp; a brass pin marks the human choice

MOTION · MUSIC

  • On-twos jitter — steps(12) with a seeded ±1 px / ±0.5° boil on every scrap — reads as hand-animated at 24 fps
  • Cut-in slap — 3-frame entry, no easing, overshoot 2 % then hold; every slap is a kick or snare hit at 120 BPM
  • Replacement swap — hard-cut swap (no tween) of the cut-out scrap for the corrected clipping, landing on a downbeat

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Collage is warm, human and fast to produce, and “we cut the wrong number out and pinned the right one” is a memorable, literal image of catching a problem. Risk: rawness can undercut a precision product — keep every number properly typeset and the anomaly scrap clean.

Adapt to your product: Photocopy (or screenshot and halftone) your own product screens as the scraps, and cut out the exact value your product flags; the human action becomes the pinned scrap.
